FLA.head: The Panthers should have the upper hand
FLA.body: Even though Florida will be without Barkov, the Panthers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, Winnipeg is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Morrissey. The Jets’ way back in is keeping dangerous shots away.

story.head: Something has to change for the Jets
paras: The Jets are winless in seven (0-5-2), while Florida has won two in a row. The Panthers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-1 in Winnipeg on Tuesday. Going in, the Jets are seventh in the Central (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Cats fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 11th).

The Panthers (1st) and the Jets (5th) both rarely ice the puck. The Jets take a lot of low-quality shots (29th). They also create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (2nd), and that sets up a fight with the Panthers’ power play (6th), which could do real damage against the Jets’ penalty kill (24th). As for the Panthers, they are the league’s most physical team (1st). They also forecheck harder than anyone (1st), and that could keep the Jets pinned in their own end.

Kyle Connor (10 G / 4 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Jets in scoring, and Cole Perfetti (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind. Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 13 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games. Brady Tkachuk (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with seven points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Winnipeg.
Nico Daws (2-2-0 / .885 SV% in 4 GS) is expected to start for Winnipeg, and Akira Schmid (4-2-1 / .884 SV% in 6 GS) for Florida.
